what_happened: The the person running Athena found two landing intents on athena/records with invalid ids. They renamed them by deleting the old files and adding new ones (commit a754ac8). The records branch is append-only, so the full-history check now fails on that commit. The the person running Athena had not read the records rules first. Undoing it needs either a rewrite of athena/records or a code change, and both are Sri's decision. No job work was judged.
cause: The append-only rule for athena/records is enforced only after the fact, by the full-history check at landing. Nothing stops or warns a hand commit that deletes or rewrites an existing record before it is pushed. Athena has no command to correct a bad record (such as an invalid id) while keeping history, so the only way to fix one is a hand git edit. That edit looks harmless but breaks the rule. The only guard is the the person running Athena remembering to read the records rules first.
other_causes: The records rules are not shown to the the person running Athena at the point of editing the branch.
Invalid-id intents could be written in the first place, so the the person running Athena had a reason to fix them by hand.
open_hypotheses: Whether the invalid ids came from a bug in the writer of landing intents. The event does not say.
Whether the history check could exempt a documented correction commit. Sri has to decide that.
prevention: Add two things. First, a check that runs before any push to athena/records and refuses a commit that deletes, renames or modifies an existing record file, running the same logic as the full-history check. Second, an Athena command that corrects or supersedes a record, such as an invalid-id intent, by appending a new record that points at the old one, so no the person running Athena needs a hand edit. Either would have caught this commit before it reached the history check.
proposed_request: Make athena/records safe to correct without breaking its append-only rule. (1) Add a pre-push check on the records branch that runs the full-history check's rules locally and refuses any commit that deletes, renames or modifies an existing record, with a message that names the offending file and points to the correction command. (2) Add an `athena records correct` command that fixes or supersedes a record with an invalid id by appending a new record linked to the old one, leaving the old file in place. (3) Make landing and history tooling accept the superseded invalid-id intents once a correction record exists. Acceptance: a test that builds a records branch containing a delete-and-re-add commit shows the pre-push check refusing it. A test that runs the correct command on an invalid-id intent shows the full-history check passing afterwards. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
